cards.text: Ben-hadad, king of Aram, gathers his entire army, and thirty-two kings ride along with their horses and chariots. They march up, surround the city of Samaria and wage war against it. Thirty-two kings, friend, and the biggest crew I ever had behind me was the dead batteries I shared a junk drawer with.
Then Ben-hadad sends messengers into the city to Ahab, king of Israel.

cards.question: Ben-hadad's messengers bring Ahab a message. What does Ben-hadad say belongs to him now?

answers.text: Ahab's silver and gold and his family
Ahab's horses and chariots and his land
Ahab's fields and flocks and his cities

cards.question: Ben-hadad's army is camped all around Samaria, and he demands Ahab's silver, gold, wives and children. How does Ahab answer?

answers.text: He agrees to all of it
He refuses every bit of it
He asks for a few days to think

cards.text: Ahab says, “Just as you say, my lord the king: I am yours, along with all that I have.” Friend, the man asked for the wallet and Ahab threw in the HOUSE KEYS.

But the messengers come back with a second message. Ben-hadad says he'll send his own servants to search Ahab's palace and the houses of Ahab's servants, and they'll carry away all that is precious to Ahab.

cards.question: Ben-hadad gives Ahab a whole week before his servants come to search the palace.
Facing Ben-hadad's second demand, Ahab summons all the ___ of the land.

cards.text: Ahab tells them this man is looking for trouble. When Ben-hadad demanded his wives, his children, his silver and his gold, Ahab didn't deny him, and now the man wants a home invasion WITH an appointment.

cards.question: What do the elders and the people tell Ahab to do about Ben-hadad's terms?

answers.text: Pay him to leave the city

cards.question: Ahab sends Ben-hadad's messengers back with his answer. In it, Ahab takes back his yes to the first demand too.

cards.text: Ahab says he'll do all that Ben-hadad demanded the first time, “but this thing I cannot do.” I don't think Ben-hadad likes that, because his next message starts with an oath.

cards.question: Ben-hadad swears there won't be enough ___ left of Samaria for each of his men to have a handful.
Ahab sends back a saying: “The one putting on his armor should not boast like one taking it off.” What is Ahab telling Ben-hadad?

answers.text: Don't brag before the battle's over
Take off your armor and go home
My soldiers are stronger than yours

cards.question: Ahab's message reaches Ben-hadad and the kings in their tents. What are they doing when it arrives?
Ben-hadad answers Ahab's message by telling his servants to take their positions.

cards.text: So Ben-hadad's men station themselves against the city.
Meanwhile, a prophet comes to Ahab king of Israel with a word from the LORD. The LORD asks, “Do you see this entire great army?”

cards.question: Through the prophet, the LORD asks Ahab if he sees Ben-hadad's entire great army. What does the LORD say He'll do with it?

answers.text: Deliver it into Ahab's hand this very day
Send it back home to Aram
Let it take the city for a while

cards.text: The LORD adds, “…you will know that I am the LORD.” And Ahab asks, “By whom?”

cards.question: Ahab asks the prophet, “By whom?” Who does the LORD say He'll deliver Ben-hadad's army by?

answers.text: The young officers of the district governors
The elders and the people of the land
A band of prophets of the LORD

cards.question: Then Ahab asks who will start the battle, and the prophet answers that ___ will.

cards.text: So Ahab gathers the young officers of the district governors, all 232 of them. Against thirty-two kings, friend, that's walking into the biggest meeting of the year with the INTERNS leading the way.

cards.question: Ahab sends the 232 young officers out alone, with no other troops behind them.

cards.text: After the officers, Ahab gathers the rest of the Israelite troops, 7,000 in all. At noon, they march out of Samaria.

cards.question: While Ahab's troops march out, Ben-hadad and the 32 kings are in their tents getting drunk.

cards.text: The young officers march out first. It's NOON and Ben-hadad and the kings are still in their tents, which is a long break even for a stamper who spent YEARS in a junk drawer.

cards.question: Ben-hadad had sent out scouts. What do they report back to him?

answers.text: Men are marching out of Samaria
Ahab is coming out to ask for peace
More kings are coming to help Ahab

cards.question: Ben-hadad hears that men are marching out of Samaria. What does he order his men to do with them?

answers.text: Strike them down at the gate
Pull back and let them pass

cards.text: Ahab told him not to boast like a man taking his armor off, and Ben-hadad's still talking like his is already off. Meanwhile, the young officers march out of the city, with the army behind them.
And each one strikes down his opponent.

cards.question: Israel's men strike down their opponents, and the Arameans ___.
As the Arameans flee, Ben-hadad king of Aram is taken captive by the Israelites.

cards.text: Ben-hadad escapes on horseback with the cavalry. Then Ahab marches out and attacks the horses and chariots, inflicting a great slaughter on the Arameans.
Hang on to your apron, friend. This story is still in the oven.
